caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:vim-4
attempts.entry_title: Voxel-based state space modeling in a visual attention task and a video game (Zhang et al. 2021)
attempts.summary: The paper's core result holds in this data: a voxel-based state space separates the task states of both the movie attention and the video game experiments, and classifies held-out time points well above chance. With public atlas regions standing in for the paper's unreleased localizer regions, the attention dimensions map onto face, body and scene areas in 4 of 5 subjects. The finding that attention sharpens state separation over passive viewing did not reproduce (2 of 5 subjects), and the paper does not say how that test was run. The grouping of game dimensions into two sets of cortical regions failed in the one player whose data could be mapped; the other player's data match no cortical mapper.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zhang, Gao, Cukur and Gallant (2021) on CRCNS data set vim-4, which holds deconvolved whole-cortex fMRI of five of the six subjects of a visual attention task and the BOLD data and behavioural state labels of the two subjects of a video game task. It recovers the supervised state space of each task, its cluster separation index, cross-validated classification and the projections between video game states. The functional ROIs behind the cortical maps are not in the data set; the cortical claims use public fsaverage atlases through the data set's mappers.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zhang et al. (2021) from CRCNS vim-4

outcomes.statement: In subject S2 the four presence states (neither, humans only, vehicles only, both) are significantly separated in the attention-task state space, with a cluster separation index of 0.75 for attend-humans, 0.69 for attend-vehicles and 0.67 for passive viewing.
outcomes.quote: The cluster separation index (CSI) is 0.75 for attend-humans, 0.69 for attend-vehicles, and 0.67 for passive ( p < 1e-5, permutation test), all indicating significant separation of the clusters
outcomes.notes: With the paper's code run on the full voxel data (R3), S2's CSIs are 0.739 (attend-humans), 0.717 (attend-vehicles) and 0.676 (passive), each within tolerance and above every one of 1000 null values under both permutation readings (p <= 0.001, the bound reached; the paper reports p < 1e-5). The median over random third axes (R2) gives 0.723, 0.718 and 0.657, also within tolerance, and over random third axes the attend-humans CSI ranges from 0.683 to 0.784 (5 to 95%), within tolerance throughout. In the human-vehicle plane alone (R1) attend-humans is 0.664, outside tolerance. The code's own attention coefficients are about 1e-13 in norm (human and vehicle about 1e2), so its third axis is set by rounding and the R3 values can move slightly between runs on different machines (0.740, 0.718, 0.676 in the first run); two runs of the final revision on the same machine gave identical values.
deviations: Assumed that the third axis of the attention state space is the one the paper's code gives. In the deposited deconvolved data the attentive conditions are z-scored per voxel within each condition, so the attention variable (-1, 0, +1) has an OLS weight of 1e-14, and the third QR direction is set by rounding. The code is the paper's method and the paper's values were presumably computed the same way; three readings are shown (code, random third axes, plane), and the outcome holds under the first two.
Permutations 1000 per reading of the claims file, so p reaches 0.001 and not 1e-5.
The state space is computed exactly in the space of the 24 PCs (helper docstring); the code itself is run for the observed values, and the human and vehicle axes of both agree to |r| = 1.0000.

outcomes.statement: Across subjects the presence states are distinctly and significantly separated in the attention-task state space, with CSI 0.66 +/- 0.09 for attend-humans, 0.74 +/- 0.03 for attend-vehicles and 0.53 +/- 0.24 for passive viewing (mean +/- std).
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a State Space for Variables in the Attention Task, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The states are distinctly separated with a CSI of 0.66 ± 0.09 (mean ± std across subjects) for attend-humans, 0.74 ± 0.03 for attend-vehicles, and 0.53 ± 0.24 for passive viewing ( p < 1e-5; permutation test)
outcomes.notes: Over the five released subjects (R3) the mean CSIs are 0.663 +/- 0.104, 0.730 +/- 0.023 and 0.525 +/- 0.260 for attend-humans, attend-vehicles and passive, within the paper's spreads. Under group reading (b) each mean exceeds the maximum of 1000 mean null CSIs (at most 0.110). Under reading (a) every subject is significant at the bound in the attentive conditions but S3's passive CSI (0.062) does not exceed every null value. R2 gives 0.658, 0.728 and 0.523; R1 gives 0.602, 0.675 (outside tolerance) and 0.492. The means of the paper's own per-subject values over these subjects are 0.644, 0.728 and 0.512.
deviations: Five of the paper's six subjects; S4 is not released.
Same assumption about the third axis as fig1-csi-s2.

outcomes.statement: In each subject and each attention condition the CSI is significant, with the values printed in Supplementary Figures 1 and 2.
outcomes.quote: CSIs are shows for each condition in each subject and are significant (p < 1e-2 or less, permutation test)

statistics.n: each of subjects S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6 and each condition

outcomes.notes: With R3, 10 of 12 values are within 10% of the supplement's; outside are S3 passive (0.062 against 0.05, tolerance 0.005) and S5 attend-humans (0.763 against 0.66). Under permutation reading (a) all 12 are significant at p < 0.01 (S3 passive p = 0.002, the others 0.001); under reading (b) S3 passive has p = 0.039. R2 puts 11 of 12 within tolerance with the same significance; R1 puts 10 within but S3 passive is not significant under either reading (p = 0.078 and 0.355), so R1 would make the claim partially reproduced.
deviations: Same assumption about the third axis as fig1-csi-s2.

outcomes.statement: Attention increases state separation; the CSI under passive viewing is significantly lower than under the attentive conditions in five of the six subjects.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a State Space for Variables in the Attention Task, paragraph 2; Figure 1 legend; Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, we found that the CSI in the passive condition was significantly lower than the CSI in the attentive conditions for five out of the six subjects ( p < 1e-5; permutation test)
outcomes.notes: At the threshold 1000 permutations allow (the difference above every null value, p <= 0.001), the passive CSI is significantly lower in 2 of 5 subjects (S3, S5) with the code's positions under both readings, every null (refitted or not) and both permutation schemes; the criterion needs 4 of 5. At p < 0.05 the counts are at most 3 (R3) and at most 4 (R1, reading b, matched, refitted). S3 and S5 have mean differences of 0.665 and 0.134. In S1 and S6 attend-humans is below passive (0.512 against 0.621; 0.606 against 0.652), as in the paper's own figure values for these subjects, and the mean attentive CSI is within 0.008 of passive (p 0.34 to 0.51). S2's mean difference, 0.0525, lies above its null's 99th percentile under three of the four nulls (0.0416 to 0.0504) and below it under the fourth (0.0562), and below the null maximum under all four (0.0526 to 0.0840), p 0.002 to 0.015. Null (ii), computed as the observed values are, gives the same counts as the refitted null (i). Measured is the count under reading (a), null (i), matched permutation.
deviations: Five of six subjects; S4 is not released.
How condition labels are permuted is not fixed by the paper; two schemes were run (matched by movie frame, and global), and the outcome is the same under both.
Permutations 1000, so the bound reached is 0.001 and not the paper's 1e-5.

outcomes.statement: Held-out TRs of the attention task are classified into the 12 labels (four presence states by three attention conditions) from their position in the learned state space at 48.4 +/- 7.6% across subjects, well above the chance of 8.3%.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a State Space for Variables in the Attention Task, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Average performance across subjects is 48.4 ± 7.6% ( p < 1e-5, permutation test, chance = 8.3%)
outcomes.notes: Mean accuracy over the five subjects is 43.7% (contiguous folds, Euclidean), 53.3% (contiguous, density), 46.6% (random, Euclidean) and 56.3% (random, density), against 48.4 +/- 7.6%; three readings are within tolerance and all exceed every one of 1000 mean null accuracies (maxima 9.7 to 12.5%). Chance under this procedure (null mean) is 7.8 to 9.1%, close to the paper's 8.3%. Per subject 40.4 to 60.6%. The first run gave 44.4% and 53.4% for the contiguous readings; the likeliest cause of the difference is rounding in the third axis of each fold's state space.
deviations: Five of six subjects; S4 is not released.
Held-out positions are z-scored with the training statistics, a standard choice the claims file names.

outcomes.statement: The human-presence dimension of the attention-task state space has its weights in face and body areas (FFA, OFA, EBA), MT+, LO, the frontal operculum and the inferior frontal sulcus; the vehicle-presence dimension in RSC, PPA, OPA, IPS, FEF and around the inferior frontal sulcus.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a State Space for Variables in the Attention Task, paragraph 4; Figure 2; Supplementary Figure 3
outcomes.quote: The “human presence” dimension projects heavily onto FFA ( Kanwisher et al., 1997 ), OFA ( Gauthier et al., 2000 ), and EBA ( Downing et al., 2001 ) ... In contrast, the “vehicle presence” dimension projects strongly onto RSC ( Maguire, 2001 ; Epstein, 2008 ), PPA ( Epstein et al., 1999 ), and OPA ( Dilks et al., 2013 )
outcomes.notes: With the encoding-model threshold (ii), the human-presence weight is positive and above the vehicle-presence weight in FFA, OFA and EBA, and the reverse holds in RSC, PPA and OPA, in 4 of 5 subjects under each weight reading (OLS B, denoised B_L, Q_S); S2 fails in EBA (human minus vehicle -0.041 with B under threshold ii). Without a threshold (i) the pattern holds in 3 of 5 under each reading, EBA failing in S2 and S3 (B, B_L) or S1 and S2 (Q_S); S3's failure under B is a near tie (0.313 against 0.314). The outcome therefore hinges on the threshold. Under (ii) the EBA margins of the passing subjects are small in S1 and S3 (B 0.079 and 0.044) and 0.24 to 0.40 in S5 and S6. The t test of threshold (ii) treats the 5400 TRs as independent and passes 57 to 71% of the region voxels; in a variant not in the claims file, Bonferroni over each subject's region voxels (1638 to 2724 voxels pass), the pattern holds in 5 of 5 subjects with B and B_L and 4 of 5 with Q_S (S6 fails in RSC), with EBA holding in all five. So the outcome does not rest on the liberal test, but it does rest on thresholding by the encoding model. FFA, OFA, RSC, PPA and OPA hold in all five subjects under every reading of the claims file; LOS-bodies alone holds in 5 of 5 under (ii). Of the other named regions, MT+ (4 of 5) and LO (4 or 5) follow the human-presence dimension and IPS (5 of 5) the vehicle-presence dimension; SEF (2), FEF (2 or 3), FO (1 to 3) and IFS (2 or 3) are mixed. Measured is the count under threshold (ii) with the OLS weights, the first reading that matches.
deviations: Assumed that group-atlas regions on fsaverage can stand in for the paper's per-subject localizer ROIs, which are not public; the claims file leaves this to the author and names an fsaverage atlas through the data set's mappers. FFA (mFus and pFus faces), OFA (IOG-faces), EBA (LOS, ITG and MTG bodies), PPA (CoS-places), OPA (TOS-places, right hemisphere only) and MT+ (hMT) from visfAtlas (Rosenke et al. 2021), whose authors relate the fusiform face areas to the FFA, the lateral body areas to the EBA and CoS-places to the PPA; RSC, LO, FO, IFS, IPS, FEF and SEF from HCP-MMP1.0 areas of the same names. Other definitions of the body, face and place areas are shown as variants.

The WordNet model of threshold (ii) follows the paper's deconvolution model (Methods, Deconvolution of the Hemodynamic Response in the Attention Task: WordNet labels, FIR delays 1 to 4 TRs, ridge with 10-fold cross-validation), fitted on the non-deconvolved BOLD of the three conditions for the voxels the regions reach. The ridge parameter is one per subject, the one with the highest mean prediction correlation (an assumption; the paper does not say), and a voxel passes when the correlation of its held-out prediction has one-sided p < 0.05 by the t distribution (the claims file leaves the test open).
Five of the paper's six subjects; S4 is not released.

outcomes.statement: In the video game task the behavioural states are distinctly and significantly separated in the 9-dimensional state space, with CSI 0.72 in subject S1 and 0.62 in S7.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a Behavioral State Space for the Open-Ended Video Game Task, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: The states are distinctly separated with a CSI of 0.72 in subject S1 and 0.62 in subject S7 ( p < 1e-5, permutation test)
outcomes.notes: With one cluster per state from TRs with exactly one state (reading b), the CSI is 0.702 (S1) and 0.582 (S7), within tolerance of 0.72 and 0.62 and above every one of 1000 null values (maxima 0.270 and 0.259). With multi-membership clusters (reading a) S1 is 0.694 and S7 0.549, just below tolerance (0.558); with the three groups of Figure 3A (reading c) 0.513 and 0.386. All are above their nulls. Clusters with no more TRs than dimensions are left out (S1 flash under a and b, S1 kill and S7 run away and kill under b). With the labels one TR later, where the CSI peaks in both subjects, readings (a) and (b) are within tolerance in both subjects (S1 0.728 and 0.760, S7 0.564 and 0.584) and reading (c) is not; the paper does not say whether the game labels were shifted. With S7's BOLD as stored, not z-scored, S7 gives 0.549, 0.581 and 0.388 under readings (a) to (c), the same conclusions.
deviations: S7 has no flash TRs, so its state space has 8 dimensions.

Each voxel of the video game BOLD is z-scored over the session, as the paper's Methods say ("The detrended voxel responses were normalized to zero mean and unit variance", Preprocessing and Visualization); S1's deposited data are already z-scored, S7's are not. Rounds 1 and 2 used S7 as stored; that analysis is shown as a variant.
The S1 video game data hold 65 min, where the paper reports 90 min for one subject.

outcomes.statement: The mutually exclusive states engage close and safe explore each project negatively onto the other's dimension of the video game state space.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a Behavioral State Space for the Open-Ended Video Game Task, paragraph 3; Figure 3A legend
outcomes.quote: For example, “engaging close” and “safe explore” each project negatively to the dimension associated with the other state ( Figure 3A ) ( p < 1e-5, permutation test)
outcomes.notes: With the variables in the data set's column order, engage-close TRs lie at -1.187 (S1) and -0.190 (S7) on the safe-explore dimension and safe-explore TRs at -0.399 and -0.550 on the engage-close dimension, each p = 5e-5 (the bound of 20,000 permutations), under both sign readings. With Table 1's order S1 holds (-0.697, -0.068, p = 5e-5) but S7's safe-explore TRs lie at -0.016 on the engage-close dimension (p = 0.952), which would make the claim hold in one subject only. With S7 as stored, not z-scored, the S7 values are -0.191 and -0.548 (p = 5e-5) and -0.018 under Table 1's order (p = 0.936).
deviations: Assumed the order of the variables in the QR is the order of the data set's state columns, since the paper's code takes the state matrix as it is stored and has no video game analysis; under Table 1's order the outcome would be partially reproduced.
S7's BOLD z-scored per voxel over the session, as for game-csi.

outcomes.statement: States of the video game project at significant non-zero positions on other states' dimensions, an asymmetric pattern found in both subjects that differs between them.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B and its legend; Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a Behavioral State Space for the Open-Ended Video Game Task, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Relationships between states are reflected in non-zero projections of states on to other state dimensions ... Colors indicate Bonferroni-corrected significance ( p < 0.01, permutation test)
outcomes.notes: Under every sign, order, Bonferroni and null-centre reading, S1 has 44 to 48 and S7 21 to 26 significant off-diagonal projections (p < 0.01 corrected, 20,000 permutations, smallest p 5e-5), 9 to 20 pairs are significant in one direction only, and the subjects share 12 to 20 of their significant pairs. Centring the two-sided test on the null's mean in place of zero changes the counts by at most one pair. With S7 as stored (own sign, zero centre, Bonferroni a) S7 has 26 and 23 significant pairs (Table 1 and data set order). The paper's matrix could not be compared pair by pair.
deviations: S7's BOLD z-scored per voxel over the session, as for game-csi.

outcomes.statement: Held-out TRs of the video game task are classified into the nine behavioural states from their position in the learned state space with balanced accuracy 32.8 +/- 3.8% in S1 and 30.4 +/- 4.2% in S7, above the chance of 11%.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a Behavioral State Space for the Open-Ended Video Game Task, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Average balanced accuracy across 10 cross-validation folds in the subject is 32.8 ± 3.8% in subject S1 and 30.4 ± 4.2% in subject S7 ( p < 1e-5, permutation test, chance = 11%)

statistics.n: subjects S1 and S7, 10 folds each

outcomes.notes: Every reading is above its null (p = 0.001; chance under this procedure 10.8 to 16.4%, against the paper's 11%). S7 is within 30.4 +/- 4.2% with contiguous folds (26.9 to 34.1%) and above it with random folds (36.9 to 46.5%). S1 is above 32.8 +/- 3.8% under every reading (42.8 to 54.6%), so no reading puts both within tolerance; with the labels one TR later the same holds (S1 45.7 to 60.5%, S7 28.4 to 52.2%). With S7 as stored, not z-scored, S7 gives 26.4 to 33.8% (contiguous) and 36.4 to 47.1% (random). Random folds put autocorrelated neighbouring TRs in training and test sets and give higher values; the outcome does not depend on the fold scheme. The S1 data are six whole runs of 325 TRs (65 min) where the paper reports 90 min, so they may not be the data the paper analysed, which could account for S1 being above the paper's value. Measured is the first reading (contiguous folds, Euclidean, single-state TRs).
deviations: Classes with fewer than 2 x (dimensions + 1) TRs are left out of the density rule (listed in the notebook); kill has no single-state TRs in S1.

Under single-state labels a class with too few TRs in a training fold is left out of that fold and the fold's balanced accuracy is taken over the classes it could predict; in the first run such a class was scored with a recall of 0.
S7's BOLD z-scored per voxel over the session, as for game-csi.

outcomes.statement: The video game state dimensions fall into two groups, dead, round start, safe explore, unsafe explore and flash in TPJ, precuneus and prefrontal cortex (default-mode areas), and kill, engage close, engage far and run away in motor, premotor and supplementary motor areas, IPS, FEF and SEF; the weights are largely consistent across the two subjects.
outcomes.source: Results, The Voxel-Based State Space Method Recovers a Behavioral State Space for the Open-Ended Video Game Task, paragraph 5; Figure 4; Supplementary Figures 4 and 5
outcomes.quote: They appear to fall into two general categories. The dimensions for “safe explore,” “round start,” “flash,” “dead,” and “unsafe explore” project on to the TPJ, precuneus, and prefrontal cortex. The dimensions for “run away,” “engage close,” “kill,” and “engage far” project on to the motor, pre-motor, and supplementary motors areas, and also in IPS, FEF, and SEF ... The weights for each dimension are largely consistent across the two subjects
outcomes.notes: Only S7 can be tested by region: S1's video game data (73,594 voxels) match no mapper in the data set, current or superseded, so S1 and the consistency between subjects could not be tested. In S7, three to five of the eight dimensions fail the grouping under every reading, where one may fail: dead, safe explore and unsafe explore under every reading, and engage far, run away, round start or engage close under some (4 fail with OLS weights and no threshold, 3 with denoised weights or with the Bonferroni threshold, 5 with Q_S under either order). Safe explore has negative OLS weights in all nine regions (-0.008 to -0.241). Since the criterion asks for the pattern in both subjects, failing in S7 decides the outcome, which rests on S7 alone. With the medial prefrontal areas (12,185 vertices) in place of the whole prefrontal region (57,895 vertices) the same dimensions fail under every reading. With S7 as stored, not z-scored, three to five fail as well (4 with denoised weights and no threshold). In the variant not taken from the paper, the correlation of S1's denoised weight maps across voxels splits the nine dimensions into exactly the paper's two groups, while S7's split into safe and unsafe explore against the rest.
deviations: Assumed HCP-MMP1.0 areas on fsaverage for the regions the paper names (TPJ as TPOJ1-3, PGi and PGs; precuneus as 7m, PCV, POS2, 31pd and 31pv; prefrontal as the dorsolateral, inferior frontal, orbital and polar and medial prefrontal areas of Glasser et al. 2016; motor 4; premotor 6a, 6d, 6v, 6r, 55b and PEF; supplementary motor 6ma and 6mp; IPS as IPS1, IP0-2, LIPv, LIPd, VIP, MIP and AIP; FEF; SEF as SCEF), in place of the paper's ROIs, which are not public.

Threshold (ii) uses the nine-state OLS model, 10 contiguous folds, one-sided t test of the prediction correlation, Bonferroni over all of the subject's voxels, as the claims file names it. A dimension counts when its mean weight is positive in each of its group's regions and the mean over them is above the mean over the other group's regions; a stricter variant is shown.
S1 could not be placed on the cortex; S7 has no flash dimension.
S7's BOLD z-scored per voxel over the session, as for game-csi; the weights are those of the z-scored responses.

findings.statement: In the deconvolved attention files each attentive condition (human, vehicle) is z-scored per voxel within the condition, while the passive TRs are not. With the attention state coded -1, 0, +1 in states.hdf, its regression weight is the difference of the two attentive means, which is zero (1e-14 in all five subjects), so the attention dimension of the paper's state space cannot be recovered from the deposited files; the third axis is set by rounding and the CSIs move by up to 0.1 with it.
The data description does not say how the third column of states.hdf codes the attention condition; the files use -1 for attend-humans, 0 for passive and +1 for attend-vehicles.

The S1 video game data hold 1950 TRs (65 min at the 2.0045 s TR), where the data description and the paper say one subject played for 90 minutes in six 15-min runs. The correlation of consecutive TRs drops to -0.44 to -0.48 exactly at TRs 325, 650, 975, 1300 and 1625, so the data are six blocks of 325 TRs (10.9 min each), the 325-volume run length the paper gives for its acquisitions. S7's 1320 TRs (44 min) match the stated 45 minutes.

No mapper matches the S1 video game data, which have 73,594 voxels; the S1 mapper has 51,608 voxels, the voxel set of S1's attention data, and the superseded mappers in Mappers/old have 81,137 (S1), 84,038 (S5) and 86,842 (S6). S1's game weights cannot be placed on fsaverage or the flatmap with the files given.

The functional ROIs, and the localizer and retinotopic mapping data the paper used to define them, are not in the data set, so the cortical claims of Figures 2 and 4 cannot be tested on the paper's regions; this attempt used public fsaverage atlases through the data set's mappers.

The S7 video game BOLD (float32) is not z-scored per voxel over the session (voxel SDs 0.094 to 1.009, means -0.059 to 0.025), unlike S1's, which is exactly z-scored; the paper says responses were normalized to zero mean and unit variance.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. The attention variable has zero weight in the deposited deconvolved data (attentive conditions z-scored per condition), so the third axis of the attention state space, and with it the CSIs, depends on rounding. Was the paper's analysis run on these files, and how was the attention dimension defined? This attempt adopted the axis the published code gives and showed the plane and random third axes as readings.

Question for the paper's authors. For the video game state space, in what order were the nine variables entered into the QR decomposition? The safe-explore position of engage-close TRs in S7 is negative and significant with the data set's column order and near zero with the order of Table 1. This attempt adopted the column order.

Question for the paper's authors. For the passive-against-attentive test (p < 1e-5 in five of six subjects), what was compared (each attentive condition or their mean) and how were labels permuted? In S1 and S6 the attend-humans CSI is below the passive one, in the paper's figures and here.

Question for the paper's authors. Were the video game state labels shifted in time against the BOLD, which is not deconvolved? The CSI peaks with the labels one TR later in both subjects (S1 0.729 against 0.691 at lag 0). This attempt used the labels as stored.

Question for the paper's authors. Which encoding models and tests set the voxel thresholds of Figures 2 and 4, and how was the ridge parameter of the WordNet deconvolution model chosen? The attention cortical claim holds in 4 of 5 subjects with a WordNet-model threshold and in 3 of 5 without one. This attempt chose one ridge parameter per subject by mean prediction correlation and a one-sided t test of the correlation.

entries.name: zhang-2021
entries.title: Voxel-based state space modeling in a visual attention task and a video game (Zhang et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zhang, Gao, Cukur and Gallant (2021) on CRCNS data set vim-4, which holds deconvolved whole-cortex fMRI of five of the six subjects of a visual attention task and the BOLD data and behavioural state labels of the two subjects of a video game task. It recovers the supervised state space of each task, its cluster separation index, cross-validated classification and the projections between video game states. The functional ROIs behind the cortical maps are not in the data set; the cortical claims use public fsaverage atlases through the data set's mappers.

papers.title: Voxel-Based State Space Modeling Recovers Task-Related Cognitive States in Naturalistic fMRI Experiments
